newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel falls on interest rate speculation.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel falls on interest rate speculation.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell sharply on Thursday against the dollar and the official basket of foreign currencies following unconfirmed reports in the Israeli press about a planned interest rate cut, dealers said.

"When investors saw the headlines they panicked and started buying dollars. We can't say yet whether this is the beginning of a new trend," said Israel Sapir, a trader at Bank Leumi. Demand for dollars came mainly from the business sector, he added.

The Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth said on Thursday in a front-page headline that the Bank of Israel had agreed to lower short-term interest rates by two percentage points from the current 15.2 percent if the government succeeded in cutting the 1997 budget by seven billion shekels as planned.
However, a spokesman for the central bank denied there was any agreement with the Treasury.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the government would be seeking budget cuts of two billion shekels on top of the 4.9 billion shekels it has already proposed to parliament.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2560 shekels against 3.2320 on Thursday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6731 shekels against 3.6490 on Thursday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9104 shekels per 100 yen against 2.9084 on Thursday and against the mark at 2.1661 shekels against 2.1561 on Thursday.
In late afternoon the dollar was still trading at 3.2560 shekels.
